A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PA-GRPO work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including matching analyses moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three model backbones and seven benchmarks, including component ablations, hyperparameter studies, CoT comparisons, and bias decomposition.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds bias-specific measurements, a prompt-sensitivity evaluation, and a qualitative comparison of GRPO and PA-GRPO.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the permutation construction, semantic mapping, rewards, cross-permutation advantage, and optimization objective. Algorithm 1 makes instance-objective calculation and batch accumulation explicit, completing the documentation of the existing objective without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: The training datasets, seven evaluation benchmarks, and task domains remain unchanged. Appendix H adds a prompt-variation scenario with explicit quality criteria and instructions to disregard answer order and labels, modestly extending the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains Base, GRPO, UniBias, PriDe, CalibraEval, and PIF; Table 6 uses this existing set. Appendix E clarifies task-format adaptations for CalibraEval and PIF, whose results already covered both task types in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds RStd and CKLD evaluation metrics and a default-versus-modified-prompt comparison on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The existing full-permutation evaluation, main metrics, backbones, and training budgets remain unchanged. The newly stated evaluation temperature is a disclosure, not evidence of a revised setting.

E4.justification: New Appendices G–H substantially extend supplementary validation with a semantic-tracking case study, comparative distributional bias measurements, and a prompt-sensitivity test. The case contrasts GRPO preserving answer A after a swap with PA-GRPO following the same content from A to B. The earlier CoT and bias-decomposition analyses are retained in the main text.

E5.justification: Appendix F replaces the unspecified 'multiple independent runs' statement with three independent training runs using different random seeds. This newly specifies the reporting practice without establishing an increased run count. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added; RStd measures differences across answer labels, not run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds comparative RStd/CKLD results across seven benchmarks, including modified-prompt results. Table 5 revises the standard-permutation entries for all three MCQ benchmarks: ARC-Challenge Acc/Con/CA changes from 81.6/93.2/83.1 to 89.3/92.9/92.6, now matching Table 1. Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and derivations are retained, with no new assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results. Equation 14 replaces the abbreviated clipping interval with explicit lower and upper bounds, an equivalent notation change. The added bias metrics serve empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: PA-GRPO addresses permutation blindness through cross-permutation advantages and consistency rewards, with evidence from three backbones and seven benchmarks. The additional analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly interprets prompt-variation results as evidence against dependence on one template and discusses why UniBias's better JudgeBench bias metrics do not imply better overall consistency. Section 5.5 also qualifies the coupled-permutation advantage as dataset-dependent. The explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies evaluation temperature zero, clarifies baseline adaptations, and explicitly documents objective accumulation in Algorithm 1. The abstract changes code release from planned to reported availability at the same linked repository. Repository availability itself cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged. The new bias-metric discussion cites works already present in v1, and the paper retains its distinction between inference-time calibration, supervised debiasing, and permutation-aware reinforcement learning.

P1.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 are rewritten to incorporate the earlier appendix analyses, while Appendices G–H receive new purposes. Algorithm 1 and baseline implementation paragraphs are edited, and acknowledgments are added. Most existing introduction, methodology, and conclusion wording remains intact.

P2.justification: Tables 4–5 move from the appendix into the main results section, with revised captions. v2 adds Table 6 and boxed prompts and response excerpts for the new analyses. The existing figures and principal table structures are retained, with local resizing and layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the debiasing interpretation through additional bias metrics and a prompt-sensitivity check, resolves Table 5's disagreement with the main MCQ results, and improves reproducibility disclosures. These are useful, bounded gains: the core experiments remain unchanged, and the new prompt test covers one alternative template on one backbone, limiting broader conclusions about prompt robustness.
